guides.title: Best Time to Visit Cape Verde: Month-by-Month Guide
guides.summary: Cape Verde is warm all year: Sal averages 25C highs in January and 30C in September. November to July is the dry, breezy beach season; whales come February to May, turtles nest June to October.
guides.html:
The short version

Cape Verde (officially Cabo Verde) sits in the Atlantic off West Africa and stays warm in every month. The difference between seasons is small in temperature and large in everything else: wind, sea warmth, rain risk, wildlife and how full the resorts are. On Sal, the 1991 to 2020 climate normals give an average daily high of 25.0C (77F) in January and 30.1C (86F) in September. February is slightly cooler, with a 24.9C average high.

For most people the best time is November to July: dry, sunny and breezy, with the sea between about 22C and 26C. Pick February to May if you want humpback whales off Boa Vista, a seasonally authorised guided tour for nesting loggerhead turtles, and August to October only if you are happy to accept a risk of heavy rain for the warmest sea of the year. If you want calm air for sunbathing, avoid counting on winter: that is when the trade winds blow hardest and when dust haze can arrive.

The seasons at a glance

PeriodMonthsWhat it feels likeSea (ocean grid off Sal)
Winter sunNovember to MarchWarm days, cooler breezy evenings, very little rain, possible dust haze December to FebruaryAbout 26C in November falling to about 22C by February and March
SpringApril to JuneDry and sunny, steadily warmerAbout 22C to 23C
SummerJuly and AugustHot and more humid, sea warming fast, rain becomes possible from AugustAbout 24C to 26C
Wet seasonMid-August to mid-OctoberHottest and most humid, short heavy showers on some days, greener hills on the mountain islandsAbout 27C, the warmest of the year

Average high temperatures: Sal, Praia and Mindelo

The table uses the World Meteorological Organization climate normals for 1991 to 2020 for three stations: Sal (the airport station on Sal), Praia on Santiago, and Mindelo on São Vicente. All three use the same reference window, but the available observation years differ. Mindelo temperatures use 17 to 21 years, depending on month and parameter. The figures are the average daily maximum for each month.

MonthSalPraiaMindelo
January25.0C26.7C24.4C
February24.9C26.9C24.0C
March25.2C27.8C24.4C
April25.5C28.1C24.9C
May26.1C28.7C25.8C
June27.0C29.5C26.5C
July28.1C29.7C27.9C
August29.6C30.5C29.3C
September30.1C30.8C29.7C
October29.6C31.0C29.1C
November28.1C29.8C27.5C
December26.1C27.8C25.8C

Nights are mild: the average daily minimum at Sal runs from 18.8C in February to 24.8C in September. Praia, further south, has the highest average daytime maximum of the three in every month, and Mindelo has lower daytime maxima but warmer nights than Sal. These are long-run averages for planning, not a forecast for your week; for current conditions see the weather page.

How dry is it? The short wet season

The islands are arid. Sal's station averages 75.3mm of rain in a whole year, and only about seven days a year with 1mm or more. Most of that falls from August to October: September alone averages 34.5mm at Sal. Praia is wetter, with 176.9mm a year, of which August (54.6mm) and September (75.3mm) bring most; it averages about four rain days in August and five in September. From December to June, monthly rainfall averages are low at Sal and Praia. The Mindelo file supplies no rainfall figures.

The UK Foreign Office describes the rainy season as running from mid-August to mid-October and warns that torrential rain on some islands can cause flooding and landslides. In practice that matters most on the mountainous islands, Santo Antão, Fogo and Santiago, where hiking trails and mountain roads are steep. Leave travel plans flexible after heavy rain, including on Sal and Boa Vista.

Sea temperature

Sea temperatures use NOAA NCEI OISST 1991 to 2020 normals, the same source as our weather page, at the ocean grid centre 16.625N, 22.875W off Sal. These are monthly means rounded to whole degrees, not beach measurements or a forecast for every island.

MonthsAverage sea surface temperature
February, March, AprilAbout 22C, the coolest stretch
May and JuneAbout 23C
JulyAbout 24C
August to OctoberAbout 26C to 27C, the warmest stretch
NovemberAbout 26C
December and JanuaryAbout 24C falling to about 23C

So the sea lags the air: it is warmest in September and October and coolest in late winter and spring. A winter visitor in February swims in water around 22C, a temperature whose comfort depends on the swimmer. Whatever the month, take the currents seriously: the Foreign Office says tides and currents around the islands are very strong, so swim where a lifeguard is on duty and follow the flags at beaches such as Santa Maria beach on Sal.

Month by month

November and December: the start of winter sun

November is one of the best all-round months. Sal's average high is 28.1C, the sea is still about 26C from the summer, and the wet season is over. December cools to a 26.1C average high with the sea near 24C. This is when the winter-sun season gets going on Santa Maria and around Sal Rei, so compare quotes for your exact dates. Project Biodiversity places hatching between August and December, and from December the Foreign Office notes that dust storms, known locally as bruma seca, can occur.

January to March: breezy, mild, the windsurfing peak

These are the coolest months, with average highs of about 25C on Sal and 24C to 24.4C in Mindelo, and night-time lows near 19C on Sal. The north-east trade winds are a constant feature, which is why kitesurfing and windsurfing locations on Sal, including Kite Beach and Ponta Preta are options for winter wind sports, and why a sheltered spot matters for sunbathing. The Foreign Office says bruma seca can happen from December to February and, when intense, can disrupt flights, especially on Boa Vista. Check your school calendar and compare package prices for your exact dates.

Carnival is the big cultural event. Mindelo Carnival on São Vicente builds to Carnival Tuesday, which falls on 9 February 2027 by the Gregorian calendar. That calendar date does not confirm the parade programme or public-service closures. Humpback whales start to arrive in February (see below), so whale watching off Boa Vista becomes possible from late winter.

April to June: dry, steadily warmer

Monthly rainfall averages are low, and Sal's average high climbs from 25.5C in April to 27.0C in June. Compare accommodation quotes rather than assuming spring will be cheaper. The sea is at its coolest early in the period, around 22C, before warming in June. April is music month in Praia: the Atlantic Music Expo runs from 5 to 8 April 2027 according to the organiser, and the Kriol Jazz Festival is also held in Praia in April. The official tourism calendar lists Fogo's Bandeira de São Filipe celebrations in late April and the Gamboa Festival in Praia in May. June brings the São João festival on 24 June on Santo Antão and São Vicente. Check edition-specific programmes before booking.

July and August: heat, turtles and festivals

Temperatures and humidity rise: Sal averages 28.1C in July and 29.6C in August, and the sea warms to about 24C and then 26C. Turtle nesting is under way on the beaches of Sal and Boa Vista, and guided night walks run during the observation window set each season. Compare travel and accommodation prices for your exact dates. Independence Day on 5 July is a national holiday, and in August São Vicente hosts the Baía das Gatas festival, held in 2026 from 6 to 9 August.

September and October: warmest sea, wettest weeks

September is the hottest month on Sal (30.1C average high) and October the hottest in Praia (31.0C). The sea is at its peak, about 27C. August to October bring most of the rain at Sal and Praia; September is the wettest month at both stations. On Sal that still means only a few rain days in a typical month. Project Biodiversity gives August to December for turtle hatching. On Sal, the Santa Maria festival takes place on the beach in September (11 and 12 September in 2026, according to the Sal municipal council). If your dates are flexible, compare October quotes and allow for rain.

Wildlife seasons

Loggerhead turtles: June to December

Project Biodiversity, the conservation group that runs turtle protection on Sal, says the nesting season runs from June until October and the hatching season from August to December. Its guidance for visitors is clear: watching nesting turtles is done only on guided tours with certified guides, it is illegal to go to the beach at night to watch nesting turtles without a guide, lights and phone flashes stay off, and at most ten people are allowed behind a nesting turtle. The public observation window for nesting tours is shorter than the nesting season (1 July to the end of September in 2026, excluding specific beaches; future dates need confirmation), so check before booking. See turtle watching for how tours work, and Morro de Areia on Boa Vista for one of the protected coastal areas.

Humpback whales: February to May

Humpback whales come to Cape Verde to breed. Loro Parque Fundación, which supports whale research on Boa Vista with the local association BIOS.CV, gives the breeding season as February to May. A study published in the Journal of Cetacean Research and Management reports that Sal Rei bay on Boa Vista appears to be the single most important bay for breeding, calving and nursing humpbacks in the eastern North Atlantic, and describes a very small population in its study of the 2011 and 2012 breeding seasons. Consider Boa Vista in March or April for a whale-focused trip; sightings are not guaranteed.

Crowds and prices

Compare live prices for several dates rather than treating a month as a guaranteed bargain. Check accommodation and transport together if you want to island-hop. Leave time between connections: the US commercial guide warns that ferry travel is subject to cancellation and delay due to sea conditions, and FCDO advises following local advice before sea travel.

Best time by interest

  • Beach and sun: November to July for dry weather; September and October for the warmest sea if you accept some rain risk. Compare the two main islands in Sal or Boa Vista.
  • Kitesurfing and windsurfing: December to March, the tourism institute's recommended window for wind-powered sports.
  • Hiking: consider the dry months on Santo Antão and Fogo, but check local forecasts and trail conditions rather than using coastal normals for mountain routes. See hiking in Santo Antão and climbing Pico do Fogo.
  • Whales: February to May around Boa Vista.
  • Turtles: check the authorised tour dates each season; nesting runs June to October and hatching August to December.
  • Music and festivals: February for Mindelo Carnival, April for Praia's music events, August for Baía das Gatas.

For a wider choice of islands, read which Cape Verde island is best, and for the winter months in detail, Cape Verde in winter. Before you book, check entry requirements and the 2027 public holidays.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the best month to visit Cape Verde?

For most visitors, November is the best single month: Sal averages a 28.1C high, the sea is still about 26C after the summer, and the wet season has ended. May and June have low rainfall averages and highs of about 26C to 27C on Sal; compare prices for your dates.

Is Cape Verde warm in winter?

Yes, but it is warm rather than hot. The 1991 to 2020 normals give Sal an average high of about 25C from January to March, with nights near 19C. The sea is about 22C to 23C. Constant trade winds make it feel cooler on exposed beaches and in the evening.

When is the rainy season in Cape Verde?

The UK Foreign Office gives mid-August to mid-October. Climate normals agree: at Sal, September averages 34.5mm of rain, and Praia averages 54.6mm in August and 75.3mm in September. The coastal station records do not describe rainfall on every island or mountain route.

When is the sea warmest?

September and October, at about 27C in an ocean grid off Sal according to NOAA's sea surface temperature record for 1991 to 2020. It is coolest from February to April, at about 22C.

When can you see turtles and whales?

Loggerhead turtles nest from June to October and hatchlings emerge from August to December, according to Project Biodiversity on Sal; nesting walks must be done with a certified guide. Humpback whales breed around the islands from February to May, with Sal Rei bay on Boa Vista the key area.

What is bruma seca?

It is the local name for dust haze blown off the African mainland. The UK Foreign Office says these sandstorms can happen between December and February and, when intense, can disrupt flights, especially on Boa Vista. Keep your tour operator's or airline's contact details handy in those months.

guides.title: Cape Verde Currency and Money: Escudos, Euros, Cards and Cash
guides.summary: Cape Verde uses the escudo, pegged to the euro. Euros are widely taken on Sal and Boa Vista, Visa and Mastercard work on the Vinti4 network, and escudo exports are capped.
guides.html:
Money in Cape Verde (officially Cabo Verde) is less complicated than it first looks. There is a local currency, the escudo, but it is tied to the euro, and in the resort areas of Sal and Boa Vista euros change hands every day. The details that catch people out are elsewhere: a fee to pay before you fly, a small allowance for taking escudos home, and cards that work well in some places and not at all in others. This guide uses official sources as read in November 2026 and says where we could not confirm something.

The escudo and its link to the euro

The official currency is the Cape Verdean escudo. Official sources use CVE or ECV for the currency; the consular fee table writes amounts in the form 3,400 $ 00. The US government's commercial guide states that the escudo is pegged to the euro while the escudo to US dollar rate changes daily. The peg comes from an exchange cooperation agreement between Portugal and Cape Verde established in 1998, so the escudo moves with the euro rather than floating against it.

The Banco de Cabo Verde states the fixed parity as EUR 1 = CVE 110.265. Its clarification on card conversion also explains that conversion services can carry an additional fee. The peg is not a guarantee of a fee-free transaction: check your bank's charges and the conversion offered before paying or withdrawing cash.

For travellers paying in pounds or dollars, the practical effect is simple: your costs in Cape Verde move up and down with your currency's rate against the euro.

The first payment: before you land

For travellers subject to pre-registration, use only the official platform, www.ease.gov.cv. FCDO advises British visitors to register at least five days before arrival, bring confirmation and check whether their tour operator handles it. As of November 2026, Decree-Law 49/2026 (in force since 4 November 2026) sets the airport security fee (TSA) at 4,400 escudos per international arrival, about EUR 39.90 at the official euro parity, and 200 escudos (about EUR 1.81) for domestic flights, collected when the domestic ticket is issued. The consular portal's FAQ still showed the older 3,400 and 150 escudos when we read it. Exemptions apply: children under two are exempt from TSA, and the consular portal also lists exemptions linked to Cape Verdean nationality, family ties, transit and official missions. Cape Verdean nationals and foreign residents are exempt from pre-registration; FCDO also exempts children aged one and under. From 1 July 2026, FCDO says travellers who have not pre-registered or cannot show proof must pay double the TSA at border control. Check whether TSA is included in your booking before paying separately. Our visa and entry requirements guide covers the steps.

Paying in euros

The US commercial guide says euros are widely accepted, particularly on the islands of Sal and Boa Vista. For stays in Santa Maria and Sal Rei, check the accepted currency with each business. Three practical points:

  • Ask about change. Check the currency and exchange rate before paying in euros.
  • Small notes help. Consider bringing smaller euro notes for small purchases.
  • Away from the resorts, think escudos. On Santiago, Santo Antão, Fogo, Maio or São Nicolau, and in local markets, shops and minibuses everywhere, plan to pay in the local currency. The tourism institute recommends escudos for small purchases and market visits.

Cards and ATMs: the Vinti4 network

Cape Verde's card payments and cash machines run on a national network called Vinti4, operated by SISP. According to the US commercial guide, the Vinti4 network generally accepts Visa cards and Mastercard, both for payments at card terminals and at ATMs for cash withdrawals, and the fees for payments and withdrawals are set by your card issuer. SISP's own page on international cards names VISA, MasterCard and American Express acceptance, but does not say how widely American Express is taken, so carry a Visa or Mastercard as your main card.

What this means on the ground:

  • Cash machines: withdrawing escudos from an ATM with a Visa or Mastercard debit card is the simplest way to get local cash. Check your bank's foreign transaction and withdrawal fees before you go.
  • Card payments: hotels and larger restaurants in the resort towns usually take cards. Small cafés, beach bars, market stalls and taxis may not.
  • Traveller's cheques: the US guide says they are not commonly accepted. Leave them at home.
  • Check with your bank. Ask about card use abroad and any travel-notification requirements.

Check cash-machine locations before travelling to smaller towns or villages. If you are heading for the hiking trails of Santo Antão or Chã das Caldeiras on Fogo, take enough escudos with you from a town.

Cash limits when you arrive and leave

The airport operator, Cabo Verde Airports, publishes the rules on carrying money. As of November 2026 its page says:

SituationRule
Arriving with foreign currency over 1,000,000 escudosDeclare it to the border police in order to use the money freely
Taking escudos out of the countryUp to 20,000 escudos in notes and coins per person per trip; more needs prior authorisation from the Banco de Cabo Verde
Non-residents leaving with foreign currencyUp to 1,000,000 escudos' worth, plus cards and cheques issued abroad
Non-residents leaving with moreProof that you brought the money in or bought it from an authorised exchange (for example a customs-stamped entry declaration)

One million escudos is far more than a holiday budget, so most visitors will never come close. The limit that matters is the 20,000 escudo cap on taking local currency out. The export cap is reason enough to plan on getting escudos after you land and to spend or change most of them before you fly home.

As of November 2026, the same operator says non-commercial goods worth up to 15,000 escudos enter duty-free, and the UK government warns that you must declare anything that may be prohibited or subject to tax or duty.

Changing money

As of November 2026, the airport page warns that buying currency outside authorised exchange entities (banks, exchange offices) can lead to a fine of 10% to 100% of the amount seized. Use banks or authorised exchange offices. If a hotel offers exchange, check that it is authorised. Keep the receipts if you change large sums.

Tipping

We did not find an official Cape Verdean source on tipping, so treat this as general guidance rather than a rule. Do not assume a fixed tipping percentage. Check whether a service charge is already on the bill. Where it is not, rounding up or leaving a small amount for good service in a restaurant, or for a guide after a turtle-watching night or a whale-watching trip, is an optional choice. Ask which currency is preferred.

What things cost, in words

Compare current menus and operator quotes when setting your budget. The tourism institute publishes broad examples, but these are not guaranteed prices for a particular business.

  • All-inclusive resorts on Sal and Boa Vista can help you plan spending: check what is included and budget separately for excursions, drinks outside the hotel and souvenirs.
  • Excursions: allow a separate budget. Kitesurfing lessons, scuba diving, desert and dune tours and boat trips should be compared using current operator quotes.
  • Local food: compare a plate of cachupa in a local café with grilled lobster (lagosta grelhada) on the menu before choosing.
  • Drinks: try local grogue and ponche rather than imported spirits.
  • Island hopping adds up: domestic flights and ferries are a real line in the budget. See our island-hopping guide.

In towns such as Praia and Mindelo, local cafés and markets give you a feel for everyday prices outside the resort bubble.

Keeping your money safe

The UK government's advice is to leave valuables somewhere secure, such as a hotel safe, and to avoid carrying large amounts of cash or wearing expensive jewellery. It notes pickpocketing, bag snatching and muggings, particularly in Praia and on Sal and Boa Vista. Carry one card and a day's cash, keep a second card in the safe, and use ATMs inside banks or hotels in daylight where you can. See is Cape Verde safe for the full advice.

Money checklist

  1. Check your exemptions and booking inclusions, then pre-register and pay any TSA due on www.ease.gov.cv. Keep the confirmation.
  2. Pack a Visa or Mastercard (two if you can, kept separately) and tell your bank.
  3. Bring some euros in small notes for arrival and tips.
  4. Withdraw escudos from an ATM once you land if you are leaving the resort.
  5. Declare foreign cash over 1,000,000 escudos' worth on arrival (rare for holidaymakers).
  6. Spend or change escudos before leaving: the export allowance is 20,000 per person.

For more planning help see local tips, things to do in Cape Verde and our 7-day Sal itinerary.

Frequently Asked Questions

What currency is used in Cape Verde?

The Cape Verdean escudo (CVE, also written ECV). The fixed parity is EUR 1 = CVE 110.265. The exchange cooperation agreement with Portugal dates to 1998.

Can I use euros in Cape Verde?

Yes, widely on Sal and Boa Vista, according to the US government's commercial guide. Check acceptance and the currency of change before paying. Carry escudos for small purchases and market visits, as the tourism institute recommends.

Do cards work in Cape Verde?

Visa and Mastercard generally work on the national Vinti4 network, for card payments and at ATMs. SISP, which runs the network, also names American Express, but carry a Visa or Mastercard as your main card. Check card acceptance before ordering or travelling.

Should I buy escudos before I travel?

Consider withdrawing escudos after arrival and bringing some euros for initial expenses. Official rules limit taking escudos out of Cape Verde to 20,000 per person per trip, so do not plan to bring large amounts home either.

How much cash can I bring into Cape Verde?

The airport operator says foreign currency over 1,000,000 escudos' worth must be declared to the border police on arrival. Holiday amounts are far below that. If you do declare, keep the stamped declaration so you can take the money out again.

Do you tip in Cape Verde?

We found no official guidance establishing a tipping amount. Treat it as an optional choice. Check the bill for a service charge first. Rounding up in restaurants and giving a little to guides and drivers after good service is one option.

Is Cape Verde expensive?

It depends where you eat and what you book. Compare restaurant menus and excursion quotes on Sal, Boa Vista, Praia and Mindelo for your own budget. Island hopping by plane or ferry is a significant cost.

guides.title: Cape Verde in Winter: Weather, Wind and What to Pack
guides.summary: From November to March, Sal averages highs of 25C to 28C with almost no rain, and the sea cools from about 26C to 22C. Expect steady trade winds and, from December to February, possible dust haze.
guides.html:
Winter sun in Cape Verde: what to expect

Cape Verde (Cabo Verde) stays warm through the northern winter. On Sal and Boa Vista, plan for the dry season, beach days and wind, with swimming decisions based on local conditions. It is not, however, a still and steamy tropical island at this time of year. Winter is the breezy season. North-east trade winds influence the climate, evenings can feel fresh, and from December to February a dust haze called bruma seca can sometimes dull the sky.

Knowing that before you go makes the difference between a good trip and a disappointed one. This guide sets out the numbers for each winter month, explains the wind and the haze, and covers sea temperature, swimming safety and packing.

Temperatures on Sal, November to March

Figures come from the World Meteorological Organization climate normals for 1991 to 2020 for the Sal station, the long-run record for the island's airport area. They are station averages, not limits on the weather during your week.

MonthAverage daily highAverage daily lowAverage rainfall
November28.1C (83F)22.5C (73F)1.3mm
December26.1C (79F)20.5C (69F)3.4mm
January25.0C (77F)19.2C (67F)2.8mm
February24.9C (77F)18.8C (66F)0.5mm
March25.2C (77F)18.9C (66F)0.5mm

Rain is almost a non-event: in a typical winter month Sal records less than one day with 1mm or more. The coolest stretch is January to March, when highs sit around 25C and nights drop to about 19C. November is the warmest winter month by a clear margin, with highs above 28C, because the islands are still coming out of their hottest season. For the rest of the year, see the best time to visit Cape Verde.

What about Boa Vista?

The WMO archive used here supplies Sal, Praia and Mindelo files, not a Boa Vista station file. INMG's climate-services page can be opened, although its home page displays a maintenance notice. Its displayed station tables use 1981 to 2010, so they are not mixed with this guide's 1991 to 2020 records. Sal's figures describe Sal, not an official Boa Vista normal. Boa Vista's resorts around Sal Rei and along beaches such as Praia de Chaves and Praia de Santa Mónica sit on open coast, so wind is worth considering when choosing where to spend the day.

The wind: great for kites, a nuisance on the sunbed

The tourism institute recommends December to March for wind-powered sports. The wind comes from the north-east across open ocean and arrives on Sal and Boa Vista with little to slow it down, across their predominantly flat terrain. Several things follow from that:

  • Kitesurfers and windsurfers love it. Consider Sal's Kite Beach and Ponta Preta for wind sports, and the tourism institute recommends December to March for wind-powered sports. See kitesurfing and windsurfing.
  • Sunbathers need shelter. On an exposed beach, blowing sand and a constant breeze make lying out less pleasant. Consider Santa Maria on Sal, but choose a beach or pool area by the conditions on the day.
  • It feels cooler than the thermometer says. A 25C afternoon in a stiff breeze feels fresh, especially after a swim, and evenings call for a layer.
  • The sun still burns. A breeze hides the heat, not the ultraviolet. The tourism institute recommends a hat, sunglasses and sunscreen.

The wind also affects boats. Excursions such as snorkelling trips, scuba diving and sport fishing depend on sea conditions, and operators may reschedule on rough days, so keep an excursion you care about early in the week. Ferry crossings between islands are also exposed to weather; read the island-hopping guide before relying on one.

Bruma seca: the winter dust haze

Bruma seca, literally "dry mist", is the local name for dust carried out over the Atlantic from the African mainland. The UK Foreign Office describes these sandstorms as possible between December and February and warns that when intense they can disrupt air travel, especially on Boa Vista. Its advice, if one happens while you are on the islands, is to contact your tour operator or airline.

In practice, a bruma seca day means a pale, hazy sky, softer sunshine and reduced visibility, with intensity varying from year to year. If you have breathing problems, bring your usual medication, and if your flight is delayed by poor visibility, your tour operator or airline is the right first contact. Travel insurance that covers delay is worth checking before you go.

Sea temperature and swimming

Using NOAA NCEI OISST 1991 to 2020 normals at the ocean grid centre 16.625N, 22.875W off Sal, the same source and grid as our weather page, the monthly sea-surface means rounded to whole degrees are:

MonthAverage sea surface temperature
NovemberAbout 26C
DecemberAbout 24C
JanuaryAbout 23C
FebruaryAbout 22C
MarchAbout 22C

These are ocean-grid averages, not beach measurements or a promise of comfortable or safe swimming. Consider a thin wetsuit or rash vest for late-winter snorkelling.

The bigger issue is safety, not temperature. The UK Foreign Office says that tides and currents around the islands are very strong, that waves can be unpredictable with a strong undertow, and that sea conditions around Cape Verde can be dangerous. It advises swimming only at beaches with a lifeguard on duty and following the flags: red means do not go into the water, yellow means you can walk in the water but not swim, and green means it is safe to swim. Take extra care on unsupervised stretches of beach. At Santa Maria beach as elsewhere, assess the conditions and follow the lifeguard's instructions.

What to pack for a winter week

  • A light windproof jacket or fleece for evenings, boat trips and bruma seca days.
  • Long trousers or a long skirt and a long-sleeved top for evenings, when lows of around 19C feel cooler in the wind.
  • High-factor sunscreen, a hat that will stay on in the wind, and sunglasses (also useful against blowing sand).
  • A rash vest or thin wetsuit if you plan to snorkel in February or March.
  • Closed shoes and a warm layer if you plan an excursion to the volcano on Fogo or the mountain trails of Santo Antão, where altitude makes it cooler.
  • Lip balm and moisturiser: dry, windy air dries skin quickly.
  • Any medication you need, in your hand luggage.

Money and entry are the other two things to sort before departure. See currency and money and visa and entry requirements.

What not to expect in winter

  • Still, humid tropical heat. Highs are mid-20s and it is breezy. Sal has its highest average daytime maximum in September, 30.1C; October averages 29.6C. These are averages, not promised daily temperatures.
  • Lush green scenery on Sal or Boa Vista. These are desert islands: Sal averages about 75mm of rain in a whole year. The dunes of the Viana desert and the stark plain of Terra Boa are the landscape, and they are striking in their own way.
  • Turtle nesting. Loggerhead turtles nest from June to October and hatchlings emerge from August to December, according to Project Biodiversity on Sal, so by midwinter the season is over. Turtle watching is a summer and autumn activity.
  • A calm sea everywhere. Currents are strong year-round and winter swell can make exposed beaches unsafe for swimming.

What winter does well

Winter is the best season for wind sports, dependable dry weather and easy sightseeing in the cooler air. On Sal, the floating salt lake at Pedra de Lume, the natural pool at Buracona and the lemon sharks at Shark Bay all make good half-day trips. From late winter, humpback whales arrive: Loro Parque Fundación, which supports whale research on Boa Vista with the local association BIOS.CV, gives the breeding season as February to May, so whale watching becomes possible toward the end of a winter trip. In February, Mindelo Carnival on São Vicente is the cultural high point of the season, with Carnival Tuesday falling on 9 February in 2027 by the Gregorian calendar. Confirm the parade programme separately; the calendar date does not establish public-service closures.

For ideas on structuring the week, see the Sal 7-day itinerary or the Boa Vista 5-day itinerary, and if you have not chosen an island yet, Sal or Boa Vista compares the two.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is Cape Verde hot in January?

It is warm, not hot. The 1991 to 2020 normals for Sal give an average high of 25.0C (77F) and an average low of 19.2C (67F) in January. With the trade winds blowing, afternoons feel pleasant and evenings feel cool enough for a light layer.

Is the sea warm enough to swim in Cape Verde in winter?

Comfort depends on the swimmer and the conditions. NOAA OISST 1991 to 2020 normals for an ocean grid off Sal average about 26C in November, 24C in December, 23C in January and 22C in February and March. Strong currents are the real concern, so swim at lifeguarded beaches and follow the flags.

Is Cape Verde windy in winter?

Yes. North-east trade winds influence the climate, and exposed beaches can feel breezy. That is ideal for kitesurfing and windsurfing, and a nuisance on exposed beaches, so choose a sheltered beach or pool area for sunbathing.

What is bruma seca and will it affect my flight?

Bruma seca is dust haze blown from the African mainland. The UK Foreign Office says these sandstorms can happen between December and February and that, when intense, they can disrupt air travel, especially on Boa Vista. If it affects you, contact your tour operator or airline.

Does it rain in Cape Verde in winter?

Hardly. Sal averages between 0.5mm and 3.4mm of rain a month from November to March, with less than one rain day in a typical month. The rainy season is mid-August to mid-October.

Which is warmer in winter, Sal or Boa Vista?

The WMO archive used here has no Boa Vista file. This guide therefore does not make a numerical comparison: Sal's station normals describe Sal and should not be treated as Boa Vista measurements.

guides.title: Cape Verde Island Hopping: Ferries, Flights and Reliability
guides.summary: Ferries link São Vicente and Santo Antão daily and Santiago with Fogo, Brava and Maio a few times a week; flights do the rest. Times, fares, luggage rules and why you need spare days.
guides.html:
Cape Verde's islands are strikingly different from one another, which is the best reason to visit more than one. Getting between them is the hard part. CV Interilhas operates inter-island ferries and CVsky operates domestic flights. Check their current schedules before booking. This guide sets out what exists as of November 2026, taken from the operators' own pages, and how to plan around it. It is about safety and reliability first: a missed connection in Cabo Verde, as the country is officially called, can disrupt onward plans, including a flight home.

For a shorter overview, see our island hopping page and the transport planning page.

Who runs the ferries and flights today

Ferries: CV Interilhas

CV Interilhas runs the main scheduled passenger and vehicle ferry network between the islands. Its fleet page lists four ships: the ro-ro passenger and cargo ships Chiquinho BL and Dona Tututa, and the catamarans Kriola and Liberdadi. The company groups its routes into lines: a short daily shuttle between São Vicente and Santo Antão; a southern line from Santiago to Fogo, Brava and Maio; and a long round-island line that links São Vicente, São Nicolau, Sal, Boa Vista and Santiago, with Fogo added on some trips.

Domestic flights: CVsky

Scheduled domestic flights are run by CVsky, the brand of Linhas Aéreas de Cabo Verde. Its winter timetable runs from 25 October 2026 to 27 March 2027. The booking engine lists seven airports: Sal, Boa Vista, Maio, Praia, São Filipe on Fogo, São Nicolau and São Vicente. Santo Antão and Brava are not on that list, so for those two islands the ferry is the scheduled link. In October 2026 the airline announced it had taken delivery of the first of two new ATR 72-600 aircraft.

Main routes, times and fares (as of November 2026)

The table below uses the CV Interilhas timetable for the current period and its passenger tariff for non-nationals, as read in November 2026. Flight times and frequencies could not be independently retrieved from the CVsky booking engine, so check your travel date before booking. Fares are in Cape Verdean escudos (CVE). Ferry fares are per person, one way; the tariff says prices include all applicable taxes. Air fares change with date and fare class, so check the final itinerary and fare before paying.

A few details from the timetables matter for planning:

  • São Vicente and Santo Antão. As of November 2026, until 24 November the ferry leaves São Vicente at 08:00 and 15:00 Monday to Saturday, returning from Santo Antão at 10:00 and 17:00. Sunday departures are 09:00 and 17:00 from São Vicente, and 11:00 and 19:00 from Santo Antão. From 25 November 2026 to 7 January 2027 the ferry leaves São Vicente at 07:00 and 14:00 from Monday to Saturday, and at 09:00 and 17:00 on Sunday. It leaves Santo Antão at 09:00 and 16:00 (11:00 and 19:00 on Sunday).
  • Santiago, Fogo and Brava. On Monday, Thursday and Saturday the boat leaves Santiago at 07:00, reaches Fogo at 11:00, continues to Brava and back, and leaves Fogo at 16:00 to reach Santiago at 20:00.
  • Santiago and Maio. Wednesday sailings leave Santiago at 07:00 and return from Maio at 10:00; on Friday and Sunday the boat leaves Santiago at 17:00 and returns from Maio at 20:00. Check CVsky for flight availability on your dates.
  • Sal and Boa Vista by sea. The fixed round-island timetable shows departures from Sal on Monday and Friday, and from Boa Vista on Tuesday and Saturday. A separate variant is marked for odd weeks; confirm the actual sailing date with the operator. The ship leaves Sal at 23:59 and reaches Boa Vista at 03:00, and in the other direction leaves Boa Vista at 22:00 and reaches Sal at 01:00. Compare these overnight sailings with flights on your travel dates.

Even the operator's own pages do not always agree. Its duration table lists São Vicente to Santo Antão at 40 minutes and Santiago to Fogo at just over five hours, while the timetable allows an hour and four hours. On the day we checked, the live departures board also showed a São Vicente to São Nicolau sailing at a different time from the fixed timetable. Check the current timetable on the operator's site in the week you travel, not months ahead.

Island pairs that work

São Vicente and Santo Antão, by ferry

This is a daily crossing timetabled at one hour from the port of Mindelo, with Santo Antão absent from CVsky's airport list. Fly into São Vicente's Cesária Évora airport (VXE), spend time in Mindelo, then cross for hiking in Santo Antão, the Paul valley and Fontainhas. Our São Vicente and Santo Antão 7-day hiking itinerary is built around the ferry.

Santiago and Fogo, by ferry or air

From Praia and Praia airport (RAI), you can reach Fogo by the four-hour ferry three days a week or check CVsky for flights to São Filipe. Fogo is for climbing Pico do Fogo and staying in Chã das Caldeiras. The UK government warns that sea travel to Fogo and Brava in particular can often be disrupted, so compare flight availability when your time is short. See our Santiago and Fogo 7-day itinerary.

Sal and Boa Vista, usually by air

The two resort islands are close, but the ferry between them is infrequent and runs through the night. Check CVsky for flights between Sal airport (SID) and Boa Vista airport (BVC) before planning a two-centre stay. Do not assume the available flights permit a same-day return. If you are on a package to Santa Maria or Sal Rei, ask your tour operator before booking, because it may sell the excursion as part of the package. Our Sal or Boa Vista guide helps if you can only choose one.

Santiago and Maio, by ferry

Maio is a two-hour crossing from Santiago three days a week. It suits travellers with flexible plans who want a quiet island, and less so anyone on a fixed schedule.

Combinations to avoid on a short trip

Linking the northern islands (São Vicente, Santo Antão, São Nicolau) with the southern ones (Santiago, Fogo, Brava) by sea means long sailings on the round-island line that run only on some days. On a trip of a week or two, fly between the north and the south and use ferries only within each group.

Cancellations, rough seas and what the advisories say

The UK government's travel advice, still current at 16 November 2026, says sea conditions around Cape Verde can be dangerous, that travellers should follow local advice before travelling by sea, and that travel by sea to Brava and Fogo in particular can often be disrupted. It also says sandstorms (bruma seca) can happen between December and February and, when intense, can disrupt air travel, especially on Boa Vista, and that the rainy season, mid-August to mid-October, can bring flooding and landslides on some islands. The US State Department advisory issued on 18 December 2025 says to exercise normal precautions in Cabo Verde, with increased caution in Praia due to crime.

The operators' terms tell the same story. CV Interilhas says that for reasons of force majeure it may change schedules and connections without previous notice and accepts no liability for connections to other services; a passenger who does not accept the change is refunded. If a sailing is delayed by more than three hours, passengers are entitled to a free meal. CVsky says that where applicable after a cancellation you may choose re-routing to your destination or a refund under the applicable terms, and that it is not responsible for onward connections on separately issued tickets on different airlines.

Build slack into your plans

  • Never do the last inter-island hop on the day of your international flight. Plan to be on your departure island at least one night before, more if the hop is by sea to or from Fogo or Brava.
  • Keep the return leg flexible. As of November 2026, CVsky lists no change fee for Flex and Plus fares, but says fare conditions can vary by route and market. Confirm any fare difference and your ticket's conditions before paying.
  • Have a plan B for each sea leg. If the Santiago to Fogo boat does not sail, a flight may still operate, and the reverse.
  • Book early around big events. CVsky reported extra demand during the 2026 Nhô São Filipe festival. Check availability for events such as the Bandeira de São Filipe on Fogo and Mindelo Carnival.
  • Do not rely on a single daily departure. Several routes run on only a few days a week, so one cancellation can leave you waiting for the next sailing.

Booking tips

Ferries. CV Interilhas sells tickets on its website, at ticket booths and through official partners, and says tickets cannot be bought when boarding the ship. Payment is in cash (escudos) or by card, and seats cannot be pre-booked. Every passenger must show photo ID that matches the name on the ticket, and must check in at least one hour before departure or risk being refused boarding. To cancel with a full refund, tell the company at least 24 hours ahead.

Flights. CVsky sells through its website, call centre, its own sales desks and travel agencies. As of November 2026, online check-in was listed as unavailable. The airline says check-in for domestic flights closes 40 minutes before the scheduled time and asks passengers who have not been told a deadline to arrive 60 minutes before; boarding closes 11 minutes before departure. The same page also recommends arriving 2 to 4 hours ahead, so confirm your own deadline with the airline rather than treating 60 minutes as a safe arrival target.

For money matters, see Cape Verde currency and money, and for pre-arrival entry registration, visa and entry requirements.

Luggage and transfers

On the ferry, as of November 2026 each passenger may take two hand luggage items free, each up to 55 x 40 x 25 cm and 8 kg; an item over those limits is charged 300 CVE as checked baggage. You may check up to two bags of up to 25 kg each, no larger than 33 x 55 x 85 cm, which must be handed in at least 30 minutes before boarding. Food is sold at bars on board and is not included in the fare.

On CVsky, as of November 2026 Promo, Standard, Flex and Plus each include one hand bag of up to 6 kg; Promo, Standard and Flex include one checked bag of up to 23 kg, and Plus allows 30 kg. Surfboards and bicycles travel under the airline's sports equipment conditions, so check them before you book if you are bringing kit.

Transfers. Ports and airports are often some way from where you are staying. Arrange a taxi or a hotel pickup for the arrival end in advance, especially for late ferries and early flights. The UK government advises using authorised taxis and notes that intercity bus services can be dangerous because of poor driving.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is there a ferry between Sal and Boa Vista?

Yes, the fixed round-island timetable shows two sailings a week from Sal, overnight: it leaves Sal at 23:59 and reaches Boa Vista at 03:00. Check the current ferry schedule and compare flight availability.

How do you get to Santo Antão?

By ferry from Mindelo on São Vicente. The crossing is timetabled at one hour, with two departures a day each way as of November 2026, and the one-way fare for non-nationals is 1,500 CVE. There are no scheduled flights to Santo Antão.

Is the ferry to Fogo reliable?

The UK government warns that sea travel to Fogo and Brava in particular can often be disrupted. The boat runs three days a week from Santiago, so if your time is short, fly from Praia to São Filipe and keep the ferry as a back-up.

Which airline flies between the Cape Verde islands?

CVsky, the brand of Linhas Aéreas de Cabo Verde, operates the domestic network. Its booking engine lists Sal, Boa Vista, Maio, Praia, São Filipe (Fogo), São Nicolau and São Vicente.

Can I island hop on a Sal or Boa Vista package holiday?

A two-centre stay may be possible, depending on flight availability. Do not assume there is a same-day return. Check with your tour operator first, keep the hop well clear of your flight home, and remember that CVsky does not take responsibility for connections on separate tickets on different airlines.

guides.title: Cape Verde Public Holidays 2027: Dates and Closures
guides.summary: Cape Verde's 2027 national holidays run from New Year's Day (Friday 1 January) to Christmas (Saturday 25 December). Good Friday is 26 March; Carnival Tuesday (9 February) and Ash Wednesday are covered by a yearly government decision.
guides.html:
Cape Verde public holidays in 2027 at a glance

Cape Verde (officially Cabo Verde) has a short list of national public holidays, mixing civic dates from the country's history with Catholic feast days. The table below sets out the 2027 dates with their weekdays. It uses the national holiday list published by the Cabo Verde consulate-general in the Netherlands, Law 69/VI/2005 establishing 1 June as a national holiday, and the Banco de Cabo Verde calendar read in November 2026. The central bank calendar is for 2026, not an announced 2027 calendar; fixed dates and the Easter calendar determine the 2027 dates below. The movable dates follow from Easter Sunday, which falls on 28 March 2027.

HolidayDate in 2027WeekdayNote
New Year's Day (Ano Novo)1 JanuaryFridayNational holiday
Freedom and Democracy Day (Dia da Liberdade e da Democracia)13 JanuaryWednesdayNational holiday under Law 95/V/99
Nationality and National Heroes' Day (Dia da Nacionalidade e dos Heróis Nacionais)20 JanuaryWednesdayNational holiday
Carnival Tuesday9 FebruaryTuesdayNot a statutory holiday; public offices have closed from noon by yearly government decision
Ash Wednesday (Quarta-feira de Cinzas)10 FebruaryWednesdayListed by the central bank subject to confirmation; covered by yearly government decision
Good Friday (Sexta-feira Santa)26 MarchFridayNational holiday
Easter Sunday (Páscoa)28 MarchSundayListed in the central bank calendar
Workers' Day (Dia do Trabalhador)1 MaySaturdayNational holiday
Children's Day (Dia Mundial da Criança)1 JuneTuesdayNational holiday under Law 69/VI/2005
Independence Day (Dia da Independência Nacional)5 JulyMondayNational holiday
Assumption (Assunção)15 AugustSundayNational holiday
All Saints' Day (Todos os Santos)1 NovemberMondayNational holiday
Christmas Day (Natal)25 DecemberSaturdayNational holiday

Neither list includes 12 September, which some online holiday calendars show as a national day; we found no official source for it as a holiday, so it is left out. The government can also add a one-off day off for public workers by resolution, as it did for the 50th anniversary of independence in 2025, so check the official gazette (Boletim Oficial) closer to your trip.

The holidays explained

13 January: Freedom and Democracy Day

On 13 January 1991 Cape Verde held its first free multi-party elections, ending 15 years of one-party rule after independence. A 1999 law (Law 95/V/99 of 22 March) made the date a national holiday under the name Dia da Liberdade e da Democracia, and later laws added a special public session of parliament to mark it. In 2027 it falls on a Wednesday.

20 January: Nationality and National Heroes' Day

The second January holiday honours the heroes of the independence struggle. It also falls on a Wednesday in 2027, so January has two midweek holidays a week apart. In the capital, visit the old town on the Platô and the national monuments of Praia; check for any official ceremonies before visiting.

Carnival and Ash Wednesday: 9 and 10 February

Carnival is celebrated in Mindelo, where Mindelo Carnival builds to Carnival Tuesday. Neither day is on the consulate's list of national holidays. Time off for public workers depends on a separate Council of Ministers decision, called tolerância de ponto. In both 2025 and 2026 the resolution gave state, public-institute and municipal staff the Tuesday afternoon from 12:00 and all of Ash Wednesday off, nationwide, citing the established practice and the place of these days in Cape Verdean culture. The police, armed forces, health services and other round-the-clock services were excluded. We had not found a 2027 resolution as of November 2026; if the pattern holds, public offices will close from midday on Tuesday 9 February and all day on Wednesday 10 February.

Good Friday and Easter: 26 to 28 March

Good Friday is a national holiday and gives a long Easter weekend in 2027. Easter week is a family and church occasion, and in the resort areas of Sal and Boa Vista it coincides with the European Easter holidays, so check flight and hotel availability before committing.

1 May and 1 June

Workers' Day falls on a Saturday in 2027. On Fogo, the Bandeira de São Filipe festivities take place around 1 May in Fogo's main town. Children's Day on 1 June is a national holiday under Law 69/VI/2005 of 31 May. It also appears in the central bank's calendar, although the consulate's shorter list omits it. Confirm individual business opening hours.

5 July: Independence Day

Cape Verde became independent from Portugal on 5 July 1975, and Independence Day is a national civic holiday. In 2027 it falls on a Monday, giving a long weekend. Check the published local programme for celebrations.

15 August, 1 November and 25 December

The Assumption (a Sunday in 2027), All Saints' Day (a Monday) and Christmas Day (a Saturday) complete the list. Check flights and hotels early for Christmas and New Year.

When a holiday falls on a weekend

In 2027, Workers' Day and Christmas Day fall on a Saturday and the Assumption on a Sunday. We found no rule in the official sources that moves a weekend holiday to the following Monday. What the government has done is grant a separate tolerância de ponto: in 2025, when 5 July fell on a Saturday, it gave public workers Friday 4 July off, and its resolution notes that it has been the practice to grant such days off when dates of national importance fall at the weekend. Any such decision for 2027 will be published in the Boletim Oficial, when a decision is made.

Municipal holidays

Municipal holidays apply locally; check opening hours with the office you need. The municipal holidays covered here from the official central bank calendar are Praia's: the central bank lists Praia City Day (Dia da Cidade da Praia) on 29 April and Praia Municipality Day (Dia do Município da Praia) on 19 May, both applying only in the municipality of Praia. In 2027, 29 April is a Thursday and 19 May a Wednesday.

Municipal holiday dates for Sal, Boa Vista and São Vicente are not listed here; confirm them with the relevant council. Sal's big municipal celebration is the Santa Maria festival on the beach at Santa Maria in September (11 and 12 September in 2026, according to the Sal council). Other local feast days with large gatherings include the São João festival on 24 June in Santo Antão and São Vicente, and the Baía das Gatas festival in August. Ask your hotel about the local municipal day if you plan to do business or banking on a particular island.

What closes on a public holiday

  • Government offices and public services may close; confirm the office or school schedule. The cited public-worker decisions exclude police, health services and other essential round-the-clock services.
  • Banks may close. The Banco de Cabo Verde calendar identifies holidays and confirms its own closure on working-day municipal holidays in Praia; check your bank branch separately. Plan cash needs ahead of long weekends; see currency and money for how to pay.
  • Shops and markets in towns such as Sal Rei and Mindelo may close or open shorter hours, especially on religious holidays and Christmas Day.
  • Hotels and resorts need individual checks for holiday service. Ask about excursions such as desert and dune tours or trips to Pedra de Lume before booking for a holiday.
  • Museums and heritage sites may change their hours. If you plan to visit Cidade Velha or the Tarrafal camp museum on Santiago on a holiday, confirm opening times first.
  • Transport needs a date-specific check; a public holiday does not confirm that your ferry or flight will operate. Book early if you plan island hopping, and see the island-hopping guide.

Planning around the 2027 calendar

The long weekends of 2027 are New Year (Friday 1 January), Easter (Good Friday 26 March), Independence Day (Monday 5 July) and All Saints' Day (Monday 1 November), plus Carnival if the usual government decision is repeated. For music and culture, February in Mindelo and April in Praia (when the Atlantic Music Expo runs from 5 to 8 April 2027) are the high points. For the weather and wildlife side of the year, see the best time to visit Cape Verde and Cape Verde in winter, and check entry requirements before you book.

Frequently Asked Questions

How many public holidays does Cape Verde have in 2027?

The statutory list covered here has ten national holidays: 1 January, 13 January, 20 January, Good Friday (26 March in 2027), 1 May, 1 June, 5 July, 15 August, 1 November and 25 December. Law 69/VI/2005 makes Children's Day a national holiday, although the consulate's list omits it. Ash Wednesday and Carnival time off for public workers require a separate government decision.

Is Carnival a public holiday in Cape Verde?

Do not assume a full statutory day off. The government granted public workers time off for Carnival and Ash Wednesday by resolution in 2025 and 2026. In 2025 and 2026 that meant from noon on Carnival Tuesday and all of Ash Wednesday. In 2027 those days are 9 and 10 February; we had not found a 2027 resolution as of November 2026.

When is Easter 2027 in Cape Verde?

Easter Sunday is 28 March 2027, so Good Friday, a national holiday, is 26 March. Ash Wednesday, 46 days before Easter, is 10 February.

Are banks open on public holidays in Cape Verde?

Check your branch. The central bank's 2026 calendar includes Children's Day and lists Ash Wednesday subject to confirmation. It lists Praia's municipal dates, 29 April and 19 May, and says the central bank itself closes when those fall on working days. This is not a guarantee of every branch's 2027 hours.

If a holiday falls on a Sunday, is the Monday off?

Do not assume a Monday off. We found no official rule moving weekend holidays. The government sometimes grants public workers a separate day off when an important date falls at the weekend, as it did for Friday 4 July 2025, but each case needs its own resolution.

Will my holiday be affected by a public holiday?

Check your hotel, restaurants and excursion operators for the date. Confirm banks, public offices, shops and any inter-island transport before making fixed plans.

guides.title: Cape Verde Visa and Entry Requirements: EASE, TSA Fee and Passports
guides.summary: Register on the official EASE platform at least 5 days before you fly, pay the 4,400 escudo airport security fee unless exempt, and carry a passport valid well beyond your stay.
guides.html:
Getting into Cape Verde (officially Cabo Verde) is simple for most holidaymakers, but one step is easy to miss: visa-free entry does not remove pre-registration requirements, and an airport security fee is payable unless you qualify for an exemption. Children aged one and under do not need the form or the fee under UK advice. This guide follows the order you deal with things, using the Government of Cabo Verde, its consular portal and the UK and US governments as read in November 2026. Where they are silent, we say so.

The same rules apply when you land at Sal airport for a week in Santa Maria, at Boa Vista airport for Sal Rei and the resorts, or at Praia or São Vicente for the less visited islands. For a shorter overview, see our visa requirements page.

The short version

  1. Check whether your nationality can visit without a visa. British and US tourists can, for up to 30 days, according to their governments.
  2. Pre-register on the official platform, www.ease.gov.cv, at least 5 days before you arrive, and pay the airport security fee (TSA) there unless exempt.
  3. Bring the proof of pre-registration to show at the border.
  4. Make sure your passport is valid for at least 6 months after the day you arrive (the UK government's advice) and that each traveller, children included, has their own passport.
  5. If a child is travelling without a parent or legal guardian, carry a certified letter of authorisation in Portuguese.

Step 1: do you need a visa?

Cape Verde's government publishes a nationality-specific visa-exemption list. British, Irish, other EU and US ordinary-passport visitors are listed for up to 30 days; some other nationalities have different limits. Check your passport against that list.

  • British citizens: the UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO) says you can enter Cape Verde as a visitor for up to 30 days without a visa. To stay longer, or to travel for another purpose, you must meet the Cape Verde government's entry requirements through its consular portal.
  • US citizens: the State Department's Cabo Verde page says no tourist visa is required for stays of 30 days or less. Registration and the airport security fee are still required, subject to exemptions. Check the current requirements before travelling.
  • Irish and other EU citizens: Cape Verde's government visa-exemption list includes Ireland and the other EU member states for up to 30 days. Check the government list for your passport and purpose of travel.

Since 1 January 2026 the rules are stricter for some nationalities. The EASE portal says that from that date nationals of the countries on a published list must obtain an entry visa before arriving, under penalty of refusal of entry, transit or stopover. The list, set by a government order under Decree-Law 13/2025, has 91 countries, among them Egypt, Mexico, Jamaica, Chile, the Philippines, Indonesia, Iran and Iraq. Nationals of those countries cannot get a visa on arrival. Decree-Law 49/2026, in force since 4 November 2026, now allows applications through a designated digital platform, subject to a security and migration-risk assessment; we could not confirm that this channel is operating, so if your passport is on that list, ask the nearest Cabo Verde embassy or consulate well before you book. The order has exceptions, including holders of a valid residence permit from an EU country, the UK, Switzerland, Brazil, Canada or the United States that guarantees unconditional readmission of its holder. This is an exception to the advance-visa rule, not proof that every such traveller is visa-exempt; confirm your case with the consulate.

Step 2: EASE pre-registration

EASE is the government's online pre-registration platform, and the only address to use is www.ease.gov.cv. The consular portal's frequently asked questions are blunt: all travellers are subject to pre-registration, visa-exempt citizens included, and even holders of diplomatic passports. It exempts Cabo Verdean nationals and foreign residents. The UK advice also exempts children aged one and under from the form; the consular FAQ says people born in Cape Verde travelling on a foreign passport are exempt from pre-registration and TSA.

When: the FCDO says to fill in the form at least 5 days before you arrive in the country. The consular portal phrases it as up to 5 days before the start of the trip. Do it as soon as your flights are booked rather than at the last minute.

What you need: the consular portal says pre-registration requires your passport data and your expected dates of entry. Have each traveller's passport to hand, plus your flight dates and the address where you will stay, and a payment card for the fee.

What you get: a confirmation. The FCDO tells travellers to bring proof of confirmation to show when you arrive. Keep a printout as well as a phone copy. The platform itself states that pre-registration does not grant automatic entry: border officers still make the final decision.

Babies: the FCDO says children aged one and under do not need a completed form and are exempt from the TSA fee. The decree exempts children under 2 from the fee. If you are travelling with a toddler near that age, check the platform when you register.

Step 3: the airport security fee (TSA)

The Taxa de Segurança Aeroportuária (TSA) was created by Decree-Law 13/2025 and is due from passengers who land at a Cape Verde airport unless an exemption applies. Decree-Law 49/2026, in force since 4 November 2026, raised the amounts. As of November 2026 the law sets the figures below; the consular portal's FAQ still showed the older 3,400 and 150 escudos when we read it, so check the amount EASE charges when you register:

FlightTSA per passenger
International arrival4,400 escudos (about EUR 39.90 at the official euro parity)
Domestic flight between islands200 escudos (about EUR 1.81)

For international arrivals the fee is paid through the pre-registration platform when you register; for a domestic hop, say from Praia to Mindelo, the decree has it collected by the airport operator or the airline when the ticket is issued. The consular portal says a paid fee stays valid for one year if your trip is postponed. Exemptions in the law include children under 2, passengers in transit, Cabo Verdean passport holders on international flights, and people born in Cape Verde with their spouses and children on international flights (Decree-Law 49/2026 removed the earlier under-18 limit for those children). The Constitutional Court's ruling 50/2026 also extends the international-flight exemption to foreign and stateless residents. Diplomatic and service passport holders are also exempt from TSA on international flights; this does not itself exempt them from pre-registration.

If you arrive without pre-registering: the decree says visitors who have not pre-registered register on arrival and pay the fee plus a surcharge. The FCDO puts it plainly: from 1 July 2026, if you do not complete the pre-registration or cannot show proof, you will have to pay double the TSA fee at border control.

Package holidays: who registers?

Many visitors to Sal and Boa Vista travel on a package. The FCDO's only advice on this is: if you are travelling with a tour operator, check if they can do this for you. The EASE portal has a separate area for travel agencies, and the decree refers to authorised travel agencies handling collective pre-registration. Ask your operator in writing whether every person in your booking is registered and the TSA paid, and get the confirmation. If not, register yourself.

Step 4: passport validity

The FCDO says your passport must have an expiry date at least 6 months after the date you arrive. Cape Verde's decree sets a lower legal minimum (3 months beyond the planned stay); aim for the FCDO's 6 months. The FCDO also warns that you will be denied entry if you try to use a passport reported lost, stolen or damaged. The consular portal adds that all travellers must have their own passport, so babies need one too.

Children travelling without both parents

According to the FCDO, children aged 17 and under travelling to Cape Verde alone, or with an adult who is not their parent or legal guardian, must carry a letter of authorisation from a parent or guardian. It must be in Portuguese, signature certified by a solicitor or notary, and give the travel dates, the address in Cape Verde, the responsible adult's name and the parent's or guardian's details. Without it, the child may be refused entry. The US State Department also says that a child travelling with one parent needs a notarised consent letter from the absent parent, or proof of sole custody. Check the paperwork for your family before travelling.

Vaccination and health paperwork

The FCDO and the UK's TravelHealthPro service say you need a yellow fever vaccination certificate only if you are coming from a country with a risk of yellow fever transmission; TravelHealthPro applies this to travellers aged 1 year or over. For health risks once you are there, see our guide is Cape Verde safe.

Customs and cash on arrival

Declare anything that may be prohibited or dutiable (FCDO); non-commercial goods up to 15,000 escudos enter duty-free, and foreign currency with a value exceeding the equivalent of 1,000,000 escudos must be declared (Cabo Verde Airports). Our Cape Verde currency and money guide covers cash limits in full.

Staying longer than 30 days

The visa-free stay is short. If you want a long winter on São Vicente or a season of kitesurfing on Sal, look at the visa options on the consular portal before you travel. The portal describes a tourism visa allowing a stay of 90 days, extendable for a maximum of the same period. Decree-Law 13/2025 says requests to extend a stay are made through the digital platform or, exceptionally, at the counters of the Directorate of Foreigners and Borders (DEF). We could not find an official page that sets out fees or processing times for extensions, so contact the consular portal before your 30 days run out rather than after.

Arriving by sea

The airport security fee is, by law, due from passengers landing at airports and aerodromes. We could not find an official page explaining how pre-registration applies to cruise passengers or yacht crews arriving by sea. The consular portal says all foreign citizens who intend to travel to Cape Verde must pre-register, and the decree requires pleasure boats to keep a list of everyone on board and hand a copy to the DEF. Cruise passengers should ask the cruise line; yacht crews should contact the consular portal. Travel between islands is covered in our island-hopping page and island-hopping guide.

Common mistakes

  • Assuming the tour operator did it. Ask for the confirmation; the FCDO only says to check.
  • Registering too late. The FCDO says at least 5 days before arrival.
  • Using any address other than www.ease.gov.cv.
  • Forgetting the children. Each needs a passport and, above the exemption age, a registration.
  • A passport close to expiry, or overstaying the 30 days.

What we could not confirm

The State Department country page and Cape Verde's government visa-exemption list were readable at their current URLs. The US Embassy site could not be opened. We did not find a clear official account of extension fees or how pre-registration works for cruise passengers, so confirm those points with the authorities and check entry rules again before flying.

After the border

Next, compare the islands in which Cape Verde island is best and Sal or Boa Vista, pick a season in the best time to visit Cape Verde, and see things to do in Sal or things to do in Boa Vista. Keep our emergency contacts page saved on your phone.

Frequently Asked Questions

Do UK citizens need a visa for Cape Verde?

Not for a short visit. The UK government says British citizens can enter Cape Verde as visitors for up to 30 days without a visa. You still have to pre-register on www.ease.gov.cv at least 5 days before arrival and pay the airport security fee unless exempt, and you need a passport valid for at least 6 months after the day you arrive.

Do US citizens need a visa for Cape Verde?

The State Department says no tourist visa is required for stays of 30 days or less. Registration and the airport security fee still apply, subject to exemptions. Confirm the current rules before booking.

How much is the Cape Verde airport security fee?

As of November 2026, Decree-Law 49/2026 (in force since 4 November 2026) sets 4,400 escudos per passenger for international arrivals, about EUR 39.90 at the official euro parity, and 200 escudos (about EUR 1.81) for domestic flights. The international fee is paid on EASE when you pre-register.

How far in advance do I need to register on EASE?

At least 5 days before you arrive, according to the UK government. The consular portal uses the wording up to 5 days before travel; follow the FCDO's at-least-5-days advice and bring proof of confirmation to the border.

What happens if I arrive without EASE pre-registration?

You register at the border and pay more. The decree provides for the fee plus a surcharge, and the UK government says that from 1 July 2026 travellers who have not pre-registered, or cannot show proof, pay double the TSA fee at border control.

Does my tour operator register me on EASE?

Some do. The UK government only says to check whether your tour operator can do it for you, and the platform has a separate area for travel agencies. Ask your operator to confirm in writing that every traveller is registered and the fee is paid. If they cannot, register yourself.

How long must my passport be valid for Cape Verde?

The UK government says at least 6 months after the date you arrive. Cape Verdean law sets a lower minimum of 3 months beyond your planned stay; the 6-month figure is the safer target.

Can I stay in Cape Verde longer than 30 days?

British, Irish, other EU and US visitors must arrange permission beyond their 30-day visa-free allowance. The consular portal describes a tourism visa for stays of up to 90 days, extendable for at most the same period again, and the law says extension requests go through the digital platform or the border directorate. Contact the consular portal before your allowance ends.
