destinations.name: Santa Maria
destinations.tagline: Sal resort town on a long white beach, its landmark pier being rebuilt
destinations.summary: Santa Maria is the resort town at the southern tip of Sal: an 8 km white-sand beach, a landmark pier under reconstruction, a small grid of bars and restaurants, and resort hotels.
destinations.html:
Santa Maria sits at the southern tip of Sal and is a base for beach holidays. The tourism institute describes the town's beach as eight kilometres of white sand, and hotels now run along much of it, from low-rise apartments near the centre to large all-inclusive resorts further out. Behind the seafront, the old town is a compact grid of streets with cafés, bars, souvenir stalls and a few guesthouses.

The centre of town life is the Santa Maria pier, the town's landmark, which a storm partly destroyed in October 2024 and which is being rebuilt, so expect works and restricted access. West of town lies Ponta Preta, a quieter stretch of sand known for its waves, and the main town beach, Santa Maria Beach, runs east from the pier past the hotel strip.

What to do in Santa Maria

  • See the pier rebuild from the seafront and ask locally what is open.
  • Swim and sunbathe on Santa Maria Beach, choosing a stretch with a lifeguard.
  • Book snorkelling, diving or sport fishing trips that leave from the town.
  • Hear live morna and local music in the bars in the evening.
  • Visit in September for the Santa Maria beach music festival.

Santa Maria is on Sal, a flat and windy island, and that shapes the experience: the sea can be choppy, the breeze rarely drops and there is little shade beyond the hotel grounds. It suits beach holidays, families with resort-based plans and anyone learning to kitesurf at nearby Kite Beach. It is less suited to travellers who want hills, greenery or a strong local culture; those are found on other islands such as Santo Antão and Santiago.

The town is reached by road from Sal airport, so transfers are short. From Santa Maria, trips reach the Pedra de Lume salt crater, Buracona and Shark Bay. The UK government notes that pickpocketing, bag snatching and muggings occur on Sal, so leave valuables in your room and use taxis late at night.

destinations.name: Santiago
destinations.tagline: Largest island: the capital, UNESCO Cidade Velha, mountains and Tarrafal
destinations.summary: Santiago is Cape Verde's largest and most populous island: the capital Praia, UNESCO-listed Cidade Velha, the green Serra Malagueta and the bay at Tarrafal. The place for history.
destinations.html:
Santiago is the largest island in Cape Verde, at about 992 square kilometres, and the most populous, with roughly 300,000 people according to the tourism institute. It is the country's political and cultural centre and a very different place from the resort islands of Sal and Boa Vista. The interior rises to Pico da Antónia at 1,392 metres, with farmed valleys and mountain villages.

History is the main reason to come. Cidade Velha, about 15 kilometres west of the capital, was the first European colonial town built in the tropics and a hub of the Atlantic slave trade; it became Cape Verde's first UNESCO World Heritage site in 2009. The Fort Real de São Filipe stands above it. In the north, the former Portuguese penal camp at Tarrafal is now the Museum of Resistance.

What to do on Santiago

  • Walk the old streets and the fort at Cidade Velha.
  • Explore the Platô old town in Praia and its markets.
  • Hike in the Serra Malagueta Natural Park in the island's mountainous centre.
  • Visit the Tarrafal camp museum and swim at Tarrafal Beach in the north.
  • Time a trip for the Kriol Jazz Festival, Atlantic Music Expo or the tabanka celebrations.

Who Santiago suits

Choose Santiago for culture, music, history and a sense of everyday Cape Verdean life, and as a gateway to Fogo and Maio. It is not a resort island: beaches such as Quebra Canela in Praia, São Francisco and Tarrafal are pleasant but small, and most visitors stay in town hotels and guesthouses. Assomada, in the interior, is known as the country's granary and holds a busy market.

International flights land at Nelson Mandela International Airport, about 3 kilometres from central Praia. The tourism institute gives the inland route from Praia to Tarrafal as 70 kilometres. Official advice to note: Canada and the UK both name Praia as a place where crime is more common, and the UK government reports that Cape Verde raised the civil protection warning level for dengue on Santiago, Fogo and Brava, so pack insect repellent. See the Santiago and Fogo 7-day itinerary for a route.

destinations.name: Santo Antão
destinations.tagline: Green, mountainous hiking island of deep valleys and cliffside trails
destinations.summary: Santo Antão is Cape Verde's hiking island: steep green valleys, cliff paths between villages, sugar cane and grogue, usually reached by ferry from Mindelo. Come to walk, not for beaches.
destinations.html:
Santo Antão is the second-largest island in Cape Verde, at about 779 square kilometres, and the one that changes most people's picture of the country. The northeast side of the island catches moisture from the trade winds, and deep valleys there are green with sugar cane, bananas and terraced fields. The south and west are dry and bare. The highest point, Topo da Coroa, reaches 1,979 metres, and the tourism institute calls its trails among the most impressive in the world.

This is the island for walking. Paths link villages along valley floors, up ridges and along cliff edges above the sea. The Paul valley, which the tourism institute calls one of the island's most fertile areas, can be explored alongside the Cova, Paul and Ribeira da Torre Natural Park and the Cova crater. On the north coast, the village of Fontainhas clings to a ridge on the trail toward Ponta do Sol.

What to do on Santo Antão

  • Follow our guide to hiking in Santo Antão, from easy valley walks to long descents.
  • Walk down from the Cova crater into the Paul valley.
  • Take the coastal path past Fontainhas to Ponta do Sol.
  • Taste grogue, the sugar-cane spirit made on the island, and ponche.
  • See the São João festival in Porto Novo around 24 June.

Getting there and practical notes

Santo Antão has no working airport. Visitors fly to São Vicente, stay in Mindelo and take the ferry to Porto Novo, the island's capital; check the ferry operator's timetable for your travel date. The UK government warns that sea conditions around Cape Verde can be dangerous, so check sailings the day before. Ribeira Grande and Paul are the other main towns on the green northeast side.

Plan for the terrain. The Canadian government advises staying on marked trails and considering an experienced guide. The UK government notes that medical air evacuation from Santo Antão is extremely difficult because it has no working airport, so carry insurance that covers hiking. The island also has beaches, but walking is the main focus of this guide. See the São Vicente and Santo Antão 7-day hiking itinerary for a route.

destinations.name: São Nicolau
destinations.tagline: Remote mountain island of Monte Gordo, Ribeira Brava and tuna boats
destinations.summary: São Nicolau is a remote, mountainous island between Santo Antão and Sal: Monte Gordo Natural Park, the historic seminary town of Ribeira Brava and the fishing port of Tarrafal.
destinations.html:
São Nicolau lies in the northern chain of islands, between São Vicente and Sal, and sees few foreign visitors. It covers about 343 square kilometres and has around 13,300 people, according to the tourism institute. The island is long and mountainous, rising to Monte Gordo at 1,312 metres, whose summit is often in cloud. Its interior hides green, terraced valleys, while the coasts are dry and rocky.

The main town is Ribeira Brava, set in a valley inland, with narrow streets and colonial-style buildings. It holds the old cathedral and the Seminário-Liceu de São José, a historic seminary school. On the west coast, Tarrafal de São Nicolau is the fishing and tuna-canning port, with beaches nearby. The rock formations at Carbeirinho, near Tarrafal, are another sight on the island.

What to do on São Nicolau

  • Walk the trails of the Monte Gordo Natural Park, starting from the Cachaço area.
  • Explore Ribeira Brava, its church square and the seminary.
  • See the fishing boats and tuna landings in Tarrafal de São Nicolau.
  • Visit the rock formations of Carbeirinho on the coast.

São Nicolau suits walkers and travellers who have already seen the better-known islands and want somewhere quiet. The tourism institute suggests taxis as the best way to get around. For general hiking advice, our guide to hiking in Santo Antão covers similar terrain on the neighbouring island.

The island has a domestic aerodrome, and inter-island links are infrequent and change at short notice, so plan with our island-hopping guide and allow spare days. Check the fare and any eligibility conditions directly with the transport operator before booking. As elsewhere, the Canadian government advises staying on marked trails and considering an experienced guide for hikes.

destinations.name: Tarrafal
destinations.tagline: North Santiago bay town with a sheltered beach and the former prison camp
destinations.summary: Tarrafal is a fishing town at the northern tip of Santiago: a sheltered sandy bay for swimming, a relaxed pace, and the former Portuguese prison camp that is now the Museum of Resistance.
destinations.html:
Tarrafal sits at the northern tip of Santiago, about 70 kilometres from Praia by the inland road. It is a small fishing town on a curved bay, with a sandy beach backed by trees, boats pulled up on the shore and a slower pace than the capital. For many travellers on Santiago it is the place to stop and swim for a day or two after the city and the mountains.

The town's name also belongs to darker history. Just outside it is the former Tarrafal camp, a Portuguese penal colony where opponents of the colonial regime were held. The site is now the Museum of Resistance, and it is one of the most important historical places in Cape Verde. Plan time for it: the cells and the information panels are sobering, and they explain much about the country's road to independence.

What to do in Tarrafal

  • Swim at Tarrafal Beach, the sheltered bay in front of the town.
  • Visit the Tarrafal camp museum just outside town.
  • Book snorkelling or diving along the rocky coast either side of the bay.
  • Stop on the drive north to hike in the Serra Malagueta Natural Park.
  • Eat fresh fish in the small restaurants near the beach.

Getting here takes time. The drive from Praia crosses the mountainous centre of the island through Assomada, and the views of the interior are part of the trip. Ask locally about shared transport between Praia and Tarrafal; a rental car or taxi gives more freedom to stop in the Serra Malagueta on the way. The nearest international airport is Praia airport, on Santiago.

Tarrafal suits independent travellers, couples and anyone combining history with beach time. It is low-key, with guesthouses and small hotels rather than resorts. Keep the usual precautions: the UK government warns that tides and currents around the islands are very strong and advises using beaches with a lifeguard, and the Canadian government notes higher crime on Santiago, mainly around Praia.

beaches.name: Baía das Gatas
beaches.tagline: Natural pools in a sheltered bay on São Vicente
beaches.summary: A sheltered lagoon on São Vicente's north-east coast, outside Mindelo, known for its natural pools. Home of an August music festival.
beaches.html:
Baía das Gatas is a small village and bay on the north-east coast of São Vicente, outside Mindelo, near Salamansa. The bay is known for its sheltered natural pools.

The sheltered bay is a place for family outings. Watch children closely and check conditions and supervision before entering the water. No official lifeguard service could be found here. Bring what you need for your visit. Past the bay to the east, the long sands of Praia Grande stretch along the coast.

Baía das Gatas is also the stage for one of Cape Verde's best-known events. The Baía das Gatas Music Festival is associated with August, bringing musicians from Cape Verde and abroad. Check the organiser's announcement for each edition; it has not always taken place on the beach. Expect the beach to be transformed and very crowded that weekend.

Swimming at Baía das Gatas

  • Natural pools on São Vicente's north-east coast.
  • Natural pools; check conditions before entering.
  • Check supervision before swimming; lifeguard availability unverified.
  • Very busy during the August music festival weekend.

Combine a lagoon swim with a day in Mindelo or a drive up Monte Verde, the island's highest point. For a city swim, Laginha Beach is in Mindelo itself, and the turtles of São Pedro Beach are on the far side of the island.

beaches.name: Bitxe Rotxa Beach
beaches.tagline: A white-sand beach west of Porto Inglês on Maio
beaches.summary: A white-sand beach west of Porto Inglês (Vila do Maio), on Maio island, before the pier. A shore used by local fishermen and residents for leisure.
beaches.html:
Bitxe Rotxa (also written Bitche Rotcha) is a white-sand beach west of Porto Inglês, also known as Vila do Maio, on Maio. The municipal and Maio Biodiversity Foundation heritage guide places it before the pier. Local fishermen use the beach, and residents come for bathing and leisure.

The beach has white sand, but no official lifeguard service could be found, and conditions vary with the swell. Check for a lifeguard before entering the water and keep clear of boats and the pier. Check current food, drink and shade options locally before setting out.

Maio is one of the main nesting islands for loggerhead turtles in Cape Verde, and the Maio Biodiversity Foundation runs turtle conservation work on the island's beaches. If you visit in the nesting season, go with a trained local guide and follow the foundation's guidance; our turtle watching guide explains how to see turtles responsibly.

Quick facts

  • Beach west of Porto Inglês (Vila do Maio), before the pier, on Maio.
  • Soft, pale sand; fishing boats work from the shore.
  • No official lifeguard service found; check supervision before swimming.
  • Plan access from Porto Inglês and check current facilities.

Check current connections to Maio before travelling; our island-hopping guide and the Cape Verde island-hopping guide explain the options. For a sheltered beach on Santiago before or after Maio, try Tarrafal Beach.

beaches.name: Kite Beach
beaches.tagline: Sal's windy east-coast beach on Costa da Fragata, made for kites
beaches.summary: A long, windswept beach on Sal's east coast near Santa Maria, where the trade wind blows onshore and kite schools teach. Great for riders and walkers, not for swimmers.
beaches.html:
Kite Beach is the name used for the stretch of the east coast just north-east of Santa Maria, part of the long Costa da Fragata shoreline. It faces straight into the north-east trade wind, which is exactly why kitesurfers come here: on most days in the windy season the sky is full of kites, and it was named as a possible second venue for the 2026 GKA Kite-Surf World Cup alongside Ponta Preta.

The beach is long, open and sandy, with dunes and flat desert behind it and very little built on the shore apart from watersports facilities. Costa da Fragata is a nature reserve that takes in the broad sandy beach, the dune corridor and the sea in front, and it is a loggerhead turtle nesting beach: Project Biodiversity recorded it as the island's main nesting beach in 2020. That matters if you come between June and October: keep off marked nests, stay off the dunes, and avoid driving or riding on the sand.

Swimming at Kite Beach

This is a beach for wind, not for a swim. The east coast takes the wind and chop head-on, and the UK Foreign Office warns that tides and currents around the islands are very strong and that waves can be unpredictable and have a strong undertow. Lifeguard coverage here has not been confirmed. Kite schools watch their own students, which is not the same as a lifeguard for bathers. For town beach services, see Praia de Santa Maria.

Getting there and what to bring

  • Reached by sandy tracks from the edge of Santa Maria; many people walk or take a taxi.
  • Bring water, a hat and strong sun cream; confirm services at the school.
  • Wind-blown sand can sting on strong days, so sunglasses help.
  • Turtle season is roughly June to October: avoid night beach visits during nesting season and keep lights off the beach.

New to the sport? Our kitesurfing guide covers lessons, seasons and what to expect. On calmer days the lemon sharks of Shark Bay are further up the same coast, and our turtle-watching guide explains how to see nesting turtles responsibly.

beaches.name: Laginha Beach
beaches.tagline: Mindelo's town beach, beside the bay on São Vicente
beaches.summary: Mindelo's own sandy beach on São Vicente, a walk from the old town along the harbour. A city beach beside a sheltered bay.
beaches.html:
Laginha is the town beach of Mindelo, the main city of São Vicente, and a practical beach option when staying in town. It lies in Mindelo, a walk along the waterfront from the old town, with a view across the bay. It is a convenient place for a beach walk while staying in Mindelo.

Because it is inside the bay, Laginha is more protected than the beaches on the island's exposed east and south coasts, and it is the practical choice if you are staying in town without a car. It is a city beach, with the port and its ships in view, so treat it as an easy dip rather than a remote escape. No official lifeguard service could be found for Laginha; check for a lifeguard before entering the water. Keep an eye on belongings, as on any urban beach.

Practical notes

  • Sandy city beach in Mindelo, São Vicente, inside Porto Grande bay.
  • Walkable from the old town and the waterfront.
  • A beach in the city of Mindelo.
  • Lifeguard availability unverified; check before swimming.

Laginha fits into any day in Mindelo, between the old town and an evening of live music and morna. For a sheltered lagoon swim, take the road east to Baía das Gatas, and for turtles head south-west to São Pedro Beach. The São Vicente and Santo Antão itinerary builds a week around Mindelo.

beaches.name: Ponta do Sinó
beaches.tagline: Sal's southern tip: lighthouse, rocks and the west end of the town beach
beaches.summary: The southernmost point of Sal, near Santa Maria: a historic lighthouse, rocky shore and the quieter western end of the town beach. A walk, not a swim.
beaches.html:
Ponta do Sinó (often written Ponta Sino) is the southernmost point of Sal, south-west of the centre of Santa Maria. Praia de Santa Maria runs out to it, and the last stretch of sand before the point is quieter than the town end, with the lighthouse, the Farol da Ponta do Sinó, standing on the headland. The original lighthouse was built in 1892; its current operating status has not been confirmed.

The land behind the point is the Ponta do Sinó nature reserve, which protects dunes, salt flats, intertidal lagoons, beaches and the sea offshore, along with turtle nesting and wading-bird feeding grounds. Part of the reserve was declassified for tourism development, and the remaining dunes are fragile, so keep to existing paths and avoid driving across them. The walk out along the beach from town is the best way to see it, ideally late in the day when the light is low and the heat has eased.

Swimming and safety

The point is where two coasts meet, and the water round the rocks is more exposed than in front of the hotels. The UK Foreign Office warns that tides and currents around the islands are very strong, that waves can be unpredictable and have a strong undertow, and that you should take care close to the water's edge on unsupervised stretches. Lifeguard coverage at Ponta do Sinó has not been confirmed. Choose a beach with a lifeguard on duty before entering the water, and stay off the rocks when the swell is running.

Good to know

  • Walk along the sand from Santa Maria; bring water and shade for the point.
  • Wind and kites are common on this side of the town beach.
  • Turtles nest on these beaches from early summer; no lights on the sand at night.
  • Plan to view the lighthouse from outside; its operating status has not been confirmed.

Combine the walk with Ponta Preta, a short way up the west coast, and the Santa Maria pier at the other end of the beach.

beaches.name: Ponta Preta
beaches.tagline: Wave spot and long open beach west of Santa Maria, Sal
beaches.summary: A right-hand point break on Sal that hosts world-tour kitesurf events, with an open sandy beach beside it. For watching and experts, not casual swimming.
beaches.html:
Ponta Preta is the black rocky point on the south-west coast of Sal, a short distance west of Santa Maria, and the beach that runs beside it. To the riders who come here it is a right-hand point break that the GKA Kite World Tour calls the iconic point break of Sal. The tour opened its 2026 season here with a world cup in February 2026, and the beach fills with spectators when the swell and the trade wind line up.

The sand itself is wide and largely undeveloped compared with the town beach, with resort hotels set back on the stretch towards Santa Maria. It is a good place to walk, watch the surfers, kitesurfers and windsurfers working the point, and see the sunset over the open sea. Ponta Preta lies within the area covered by the Ponta do Sinó nature reserve, which protects dunes, beaches and turtle nesting grounds on this corner of the island.

Is it safe to swim at Ponta Preta?

Often not. This is an exposed west-facing coast that takes the full Atlantic swell, and the same waves that bring the riders bring strong shore break and pull. The UK Foreign Office warns that tides and currents around the islands are very strong, that waves can be unpredictable and have a strong undertow, and that you should take care even walking close to the water's edge on unsupervised stretches of beach. Lifeguard coverage here has not been confirmed. On a swell day, stay out of the water unless you are an experienced surfer who knows the spot, and treat red and yellow flags anywhere on Sal as a firm no to swimming.

Practical notes

  • Reached on foot or by a short taxi ride from Santa Maria.
  • Do not rely on services away from the hotels: bring water and shade.
  • Loggerhead turtles nest here in summer and autumn; the 2020 conservation report records nests moved to hatcheries because of light pollution or dog predation, so avoid night beach visits during nesting season and keep lights off the beach.
  • The wave breaks along a rocky point: watersports here are for experienced riders.

For town beach services head back to Praia de Santa Maria. Read our guides to surfing, kitesurfing and windsurfing in Cape Verde before you hire a board.

beaches.name: Praia da Varandinha
beaches.tagline: Remote south-west Boa Vista beach under the Varandinha headland
beaches.summary: An isolated beach on Boa Vista's south-west coast, north of the Ponta Varandinha headland, inside the Morro de Areia reserve. Dramatic and empty; not a safe swim.
beaches.html:
Praia da Varandinha lies on the south-west coast of Boa Vista, just north of the rocky headland of Ponta Varandinha, between Praia de Chaves and Praia de Santa Mónica. It sits inside the Morro de Areia nature reserve, a protected stretch of dunes, beaches and sea that shelters nesting turtles and seabirds, so there is no development on the shore and the land behind it is sand and rock.

The appeal is the setting: pale sand against dark rock, sea-cut caves and ledges in the headland, and very few people. Arrange suitable transport along the unpaved tracks of the south-west, often as part of a day that also takes in Santa Mónica. Bring water and shade, and leave nothing behind.

Is it safe to swim at Varandinha?

Generally no. The beach is open to the Atlantic swell, with strong currents and shore break, and lifeguard coverage here has not been confirmed. The UK Foreign Office warns that tides and currents around the islands are very strong, that waves can be unpredictable and have a strong undertow, and that you should take care close to the water's edge on unsupervised stretches of beach. Its advice is to swim only where a lifeguard is on duty. At Varandinha, look and walk, keep back from the rocks when waves are washing over them, and save swimming for somewhere supervised.

Practical notes

  • Do not rely on facilities being available; bring what you need.
  • Access is by unpaved tracks: confirm a suitable vehicle and route with a local driver.
  • Part of a nature reserve: avoid driving on the sand or dunes.
  • Turtles nest on Boa Vista from about June to October: no lights or fires on the beach.

Read more about the Morro de Areia Nature Reserve, and see our desert and dune tours page for ways to reach this coast without driving yourself.

beaches.name: Praia de Chaves
beaches.tagline: Long west-coast beach near Rabil with dunes and an old factory chimney
beaches.summary: A stretch of white sand on Boa Vista's west coast near Rabil, with resorts at the north end, dunes and a reserve to the south. Best for walking; the sea is often rough.
beaches.html:
Praia de Chaves (also called Praia da Chave) runs down the west coast of Boa Vista, close to the small town of Rabil and a short drive south of Sal Rei. Hotels back parts of this coast; the Morro de Areia nature reserve extends from Chaves towards Santa Mónica, where white dunes roll down to the sand and the coast stays empty.

The landmark is the tall brick chimney of an old ceramics factory standing near the back of the beach, a ruin half buried by drifting sand and visible from a long way off. It makes a good target for a walk from the resort end. Further south the dunes of Morro de Areia rise behind the beach, and the walk can be continued on towards Varandinha if you have the time, the water and the shoes for it.

Swimming at Chaves

This is an open west-facing Atlantic beach, and on many days the wind and swell make the sea rough, with shore break and a pull back from the beach. The UK Foreign Office warns that tides and currents around the islands are very strong and that waves can be unpredictable and have a strong undertow. It advises swimming only where a lifeguard is on duty and respecting the warning flags (red: do not go in the water; yellow: you may walk in the water but not swim; green: safe to swim). Lifeguard coverage here has not been confirmed; ask on the day and follow the warning flags.

Good to know

  • Ask your accommodation about beach services, access and any charges before setting out.
  • Respect reserve signs, keep off the dunes and avoid driving on the sand.
  • Loggerhead turtles nest on Boa Vista from about June to October: avoid night beach visits during nesting season and keep lights off the beach.
  • Take water and sun protection for the walk to the chimney.

For a beach close to town, see Praia de Estoril in Sal Rei. See also the Morro de Areia Nature Reserve and our Sal or Boa Vista comparison.

beaches.name: Praia de Estoril
beaches.tagline: Sal Rei's town beach, facing the Ilhéu de Sal Rei
beaches.summary: The beach just south of Sal Rei's centre on Boa Vista, looking out to the Ilhéu de Sal Rei. Walkable from town, with cafes nearby and boards on the water when it blows.
beaches.html:
Praia de Estoril is the beach of Sal Rei, the main town of Boa Vista. It curves south from the edge of the town centre along Sal Rei bay, looking straight out to the Ilhéu de Sal Rei, the low islet offshore where the ruins of the Forte Duque de Bragança, built to defend the town, still stand. If you are staying in Sal Rei rather than at one of the big resorts, this is your everyday beach: you can walk down from town and be back for lunch.

The beach faces the offshore islet, with an outlook different from the open west coast at Praia de Chaves. The same steady trade wind still blows across the bay, and windsurfers and kitesurfers use it on breezy days. The sand is pale and soft, and the town's cafes and restaurants are a short walk inland.

Swimming and safety

Calmer is not the same as safe. The UK Foreign Office warns that tides and currents around the islands are very strong and that waves can be unpredictable and have a strong undertow, and it advises swimming only where a lifeguard is on duty. Lifeguard coverage on Praia de Estoril has not been confirmed. Enter the water only where a lifeguard is on duty, watch out for boards and boats, and do not swim under red or yellow flags.

Before you go

  • Walkable from the centre of Sal Rei; street parking in town.
  • Cafes and restaurants are in town, a short walk from the sand.
  • Little natural shade: bring your own or plan around the midday sun.
  • Loggerhead turtles nest on Boa Vista from about June to October: avoid night beach visits during nesting season and keep lights off the beach.

Sal Rei is also the base for trips to the Cabo Santa Maria shipwreck, the Deserto de Viana and, in season, whale watching and turtle watching. Our 5-day Boa Vista itinerary fits them together.

beaches.name: Praia de Santa Maria
beaches.tagline: Sal's main town beach, from the Santa Maria pier to Ponta do Sinó
beaches.summary: The beach in front of Santa Maria on Sal: a stretch of pale sand from the town pier to Ponta do Sinó, with bars, hotels and watersports along most of it.
beaches.html:
Praia de Santa Maria is the town beach of Santa Maria on Sal. It runs along the south coast of the island, from the centre of Santa Maria in the east to Ponta do Sinó, the southernmost point of Sal, in the south-west, with pale sand along the shore. Hotels, beach bars and restaurants back much of it, and the town is a short walk away, so you can spend a day here without a car or a taxi.

The eastern end is beside the town. The Santa Maria pier stands where salt was once shipped out of the town, which was founded in 1830 around salt production, and fishing boats work around it. West of the pier the hotel frontage takes over, and the beach widens as it bends towards the lighthouse at Ponta do Sinó. Kitesurfers and windsurfers use this side of the island too, so expect sails offshore on windy days.

Swimming and safety

The beach faces south but is still open Atlantic. The UK Foreign Office warns that tides and currents around the islands are very strong and that waves can be unpredictable and have a strong undertow. It advises swimming only where a lifeguard is on duty, following the lifeguard's instructions and respecting the warning flags: red means do not go in the water, yellow means you may walk in the water but not swim, and green means it is safe to swim. Lifeguard coverage here has not been confirmed; check on the day before entering the water.

Before you go

  • Ask locally about beach access and any charges for beach services.
  • Bars, restaurants and shops are a short walk away in town.
  • Loggerhead turtles nest on Sal in summer and autumn, and the 2020 conservation report records nests moved to protected hatcheries because of light pollution or dog predation, so keep lights off the sand at night.
  • The Santa Maria music festival is held on this beach each September: see Santa Maria Festival.

From here the quieter Ponta Preta is a short walk west, and Kite Beach is on the east coast just outside town. For more on the island, see our Sal guide and things to do in Sal.

beaches.name: Praia de Santa Mónica
beaches.tagline: Boa Vista's long, empty south-west beach beside a nature reserve
beaches.summary: A very long, undeveloped sweep of white sand on Boa Vista's south-west coast near Povoação Velha. Spectacular to walk; often too rough for a safe swim.
beaches.html:
Praia de Santa Mónica is the great empty beach of Boa Vista, a long sweep of white sand on the island's south-west coast. Povoação Velha is inland to the north, and there is almost nothing built along the shore: just sand, low dunes and the open Atlantic. The southern end of the Morro de Areia nature reserve reaches the beach, protecting the dunes, endemic birds and nesting turtles of this coast.

Arrange suitable transport for the unpaved tracks across the island, for example a guided tour or a vehicle suited to the route. The reward is a beach where you can walk for a long way without meeting anyone. Bring water, food and shade, and confirm any services and transport before setting out.

Is it safe to swim at Santa Mónica?

Often not. The beach is exposed to the full Atlantic swell, with strong shore break and currents on many days, and lifeguard coverage here has not been confirmed. The UK Foreign Office warns that tides and currents around the islands are very strong, that waves can be unpredictable and have a strong undertow, and that you should take care even walking close to the water's edge on unsupervised stretches of beach. Its advice is to swim only where a lifeguard is on duty. Do not enter the water unless a lifeguard is on duty, and follow the flags and local advice.

Before you go

  • Do not rely on facilities being open: carry water, food, shade and a charged phone.
  • Access is by unpaved tracks; a 4x4 or an organised tour is the safer option.
  • Loggerhead turtles nest on Boa Vista from about June to October: avoid lights, fires and driving on the sand.
  • Tell someone where you are going if you drive out alone.

Pair the trip with the dunes of the Deserto de Viana or the Morro de Areia Nature Reserve. Our things to do in Boa Vista guide and desert and dune tours page cover the island's other wild corners.

beaches.name: Quebra Canela Beach
beaches.tagline: Praia's city beach, a short ride from the Plateau
beaches.summary: The popular town beach of Praia, Cape Verde's capital on Santiago. A small sandy cove with city amenities nearby, easy to reach from the city centre.
beaches.html:
Quebra Canela is a city beach in Praia. It lies in the neighbourhood of the same name in the south of the capital, on Santiago, a taxi ride from the old town on the Plateau. The beach is a small sandy cove backed by the seafront road. A municipal record documents esplanade rights here; check current services and opening locally.

This is an urban beach: expect a social rather than remote setting. It suits a swim and a break between sightseeing in the capital rather than a full beach day. No official lifeguard service could be found for Quebra Canela, so check for a lifeguard before entering the water; the UK government's travel advice warns that waves can be unpredictable with a strong undertow. Keep valuables to a minimum, as you would on any city beach.

Good to know

  • Small sandy city cove in southern Praia, Santiago.
  • The municipal record documents esplanade rights on the seafront; check current opening locally.
  • Check local conditions and supervision before swimming.
  • Lifeguard availability unverified; check before swimming.

Quebra Canela pairs easily with a morning on the Plateau, and the UNESCO World Heritage site of Cidade Velha is a short drive west along the coast. For a quieter, wilder beach near the capital, head north-east to São Francisco Beach. Arriving by air, the beach is reachable by taxi from Praia airport.

beaches.name: São Francisco Beach
beaches.tagline: A wilder sandy bay just north-east of Praia
beaches.summary: A sandy beach on São Francisco Bay, outside Praia on Santiago. Quieter than the city beaches, with open water that needs care.
beaches.html:
São Francisco Beach lies on São Francisco Bay, on the south-east coast of Santiago, outside Praia, within the capital's municipality. The shore is a sweep of pale sand. It offers a change of scene from the city beach at Quebra Canela.

The bay faces the open Atlantic and is not a sheltered lagoon, so conditions change with the swell and the wind. Do not judge swimming safety from the appearance of the water alone. No official lifeguard service could be found here, and the UK government's travel advice warns that tides and currents around the islands are very strong and that you should take care along unsupervised stretches of beach. Bring water and sun protection, and arrange transport and a return pick-up. Current facilities have not been verified.

What to expect

  • Wide sandy bay on Santiago's south-east coast, near Praia.
  • Open Atlantic water: calm some days, rough on others.
  • No official lifeguard service found; check supervision before swimming.
  • Current facilities not verified: bring water, food and shade.

São Francisco makes a good half-day escape from Praia, combined with the old town on the Plateau. For a sheltered bay further away, the bay at Tarrafal Beach on the north-west coast is another option to consider. Read our Cape Verde safety guide before swimming on unsupervised beaches.

beaches.name: São Pedro Beach
beaches.tagline: Fishing village beach on São Vicente, known for turtles and wind
beaches.summary: A long sandy beach by the fishing village of São Pedro, next to São Vicente's airport. Known for green turtles in the bay and for water sports.
beaches.html:
São Pedro Beach runs along the south-west coast of São Vicente in front of the fishing village of São Pedro, near the island's international airport, Cesária Évora International. It is a long stretch of sand near the walking route to the Dona Amélia lighthouse, and it is a short drive south-west of Mindelo. São Pedro is a fishing community.

São Pedro is known for sea turtles that come close to the shore near the fishing boats. The conservation group Biosfera monitors green turtles in the bay and studies the impact of artificial feeding. Ask a trained local guide about responsible observation, and read our turtle watching guide first.

The beach is also exposed. Water sports take place here, but conditions need checking locally. No official lifeguard service could be found, and the UK government's travel advice warns that tides and currents around the islands are very strong. The UK government advises using beaches where a lifeguard is on duty; check locally before entering the water.

Know before you go

  • Long sandy beach by São Pedro village, next to the airport.
  • Sea turtles come close to shore near the fishing boats.
  • Check conditions locally before any water activity.
  • No official lifeguard service found.

São Pedro is an easy stop on the way to or from the airport. Read the guides to windsurfing and kitesurfing. For calmer water, try Laginha Beach in Mindelo or the sheltered lagoon at Baía das Gatas.

beaches.name: Tarrafal Beach
beaches.tagline: Santiago's sheltered white-sand bay below Monte Graciosa
beaches.summary: A curve of pale sand on Tarrafal Bay, on the north-west coast of Santiago. Calm, sheltered water, palms and fishing boats give it a sheltered setting.
beaches.html:
Tarrafal Beach sits at the edge of the town of Tarrafal, on the north-west coast of Santiago, the largest island of Cape Verde. The beach lines the shore of Tarrafal Bay, with Monte Graciosa behind it. Pale sand and palms give the beach its distinctive setting.

The official tourism site describes a sheltered bay with calm water. The mood is local and unhurried. No official lifeguard service could be found for the beach, so check for a lifeguard before entering the water; the UK government's travel advice notes that tides and currents around the islands can be very strong.

Before you go

  • Pale sand on a sheltered bay on Santiago's north-west coast.
  • Usually calm water inside the bay; no official lifeguard service found.
  • Keep clear of any fishing boats using the beach.
  • Restaurants are nearby in Tarrafal town.

Tarrafal is a long drive across the island from Praia and the Praia airport, so allow time for the journey. Also consider the former Tarrafal concentration camp, now the Museum of Resistance, and the mountain trails of Serra Malagueta Natural Park offer another excursion on Santiago. The Santiago and Fogo itinerary shows how to fit the beach into a week on Santiago.
